The Austrian government has today announced that the childhood home of Adolf Hitler is to be demolished. Hitler spent the first few weeks of his life living in the home, located in Braunau am Inn. The owner of the house, Gerlinde Pommer, had leased the property to the government, where it had been used as a disability centre. However, it has been empty since a dispute over renovation with Pommer in 2011. Pommer is expected to be given substantial compensation as part of the plans to demolish the home.

There has been a mixed reception on the news by the public. While many are glad to erase Hitler's connection to Austria, there are sections of society that oppose the move. Government spokesman Karl-Heinz Grundboeck stated that the site was 'a focal point for Nazi sympathisers' and that the only way to prevent the buildings use by Neo-Nazis was to demolish it. Local residents have said that the building is regularly visited by supporters of Hitler's regime, despite it being unmarked. The only evidence is a small memorial commemorating the millions killed by fascist regimes.

However, there have been several opponents to the decision to demolish the building. One of these include the leader of the right wing Freedom Party, Heinz-Christian Strache. He has released a statement in response to the governments decision. 'Austria has a long and proud history. However, as with all countries, there are aspects that we would all like to forget. There is a lot to be learnt from our countries history. There is nothing to be learnt from trying to erase it. As the saying goes 'those who don't learn from history are doomed to repeat it'.
